key_insight: Combining short-term episodic context with a persistent world representation lets curiosity-driven agents remember what they've already explored, preventing local loop exploitation and enabling effective long-horizon 3D exploration.
problem_solved: Curiosity-based agents in photorealistic 3D environments forget prior visits and get trapped in local revisitation loops, yielding poor coverage and inefficient learning across episodes.
method: Maintain an episodic context (short-term memory) of recent observations to guide immediate exploratory behavior and avoid re-exploring the same local trajectories.
Build and consult a persistent world representation (long-term memory or map/embedding store) across episodes so intrinsic rewards reflect true novelty over time, not just within an episode.
Combine predictive-model-based intrinsic rewards with memory-aware novelty scoring to prioritize unexplored regions and improve sample-efficient coverage in complex 3D simulators.
impact: This approach makes intrinsic-motivation exploration scalable and reliable in realistic 3D settings, improving sample efficiency and coverage for downstream long-horizon tasks in embodied and photorealistic environments.

paper_title: Remember to be Curious: Episodic Context and Persistent Worlds for 3D Exploration
paper_authors: Lily Goli, Justin Kerr, Daniele Reda, Alec Jacobson, Andrea Tagliasacchi
